full_judgment:
6. Mr. Miftauddin Ahmed, the learned Advocate appearing on behalf of the defendant petitioner bank submits that Regulation 13 of the said Regulations authorises defendant-opposite party bank to terminate service of any permanent employee on payment of notice pay without assigning any reason. Hence the defendant-opposite party bank having terminated the services of the plaintiff opposite party on payment of the pay for the notice period without any show cause notice has validly terminated the services of the plaintiff-opposite party. It is next contended by the learned Advocate for the defendant-petitioner bank that since the plaintiff-opposite party admits in paragraph 3 of the plaint that he was informed about his termination on 24-9-81 he should have filed the suit within six years from that date. But the plaintiff opposite party having failed to do so the suit is barred by limitation in terms of Article 120 of the Limitation Act. It is further contended by the learned Advocate that since the plaintiff-opposite party failed to show that he was ever refused payment of termination benefits, the offer made by the defendant-petitioner bank to receive his termination benefits from the accounts department of the bank after adjustment of any dues amounts to sufficient compliance regarding payments for the notice period as contemplated under Regulation 13(2) of the said Regulations. 

 12. With regard to the contention that the suit is time barred I agree with the submission of the learned Advocate for the defendant-petitioner bank that the suit ought to have been filed by the plaintiff-opposite party within 6 years from the date of his knowledge ie 24-9-81. The plaintiff-opposite party having failed to do so the suit is barred by limitation. Plaintiff-opposite party cannot be expected as a reasonable man to wait for long 7 (seven) years to seek his remedy by filing the suit as he did. Since it is a case of termination without any accusation such as illegal strike or abstention from work the review committee had no jurisdiction to consider the application of the plaintiff-opposite party. In this background of the case, both the trial Court as well as the appellate Court below decreed the suit on misconception of the law involved i.e. Regulation 13(2) of the said Regulations as well as misconstruction of the impugned letter of termination. In the result, the Rule is made absolute without any order as to costs. Judgment and decree dated 14-2-94 passed by the learned Subordinate Judge, Cox's Bazar, in Title Appeal No. 95 of 1990 and the judgment and decree dated 31-7-90 passed by the learned Assistant Judge, Additional Court, Cox's Bazar, in Other Class Suit No. 26 of 1988 are set aside.
